what: From a requirement that states how a failure must be handled, to the call the change was made at, to a listed defect candidate — with no place named on the command line and nothing but Jev asked.
holds: Everything each run recorded about every call it asked about: the mapping (verdict, probability, every option) and the reading (observation, probability, every option) for all 38 calls per branch, every finding, every note, and the per-requirement counts. The scoring below can be recomputed from this file alone. What it does not hold is the evidence packets — the function bodies that were sent — which are built from git objects at the pinned commits and are reproducible from them.
reproduce: node bench/replay-scoring.ts bench/logs/stated-requirements-v1.json — reads this file only, sends nothing, and prints the same table.

findings.quote: If reading an existing integrity baseline fails, the baseline-loading operation must return an error to its caller. It must not return a successful result saying that no baseline exists.
findings.condition: Execution reaches the call `crate::atomic_file::read_to_string_capped(&path, MAX_TRACKED_FILE_BYTES)` inside `read_baseline`. There, `crate::atomic_file::read_to_string_capped(&path, MAX_TRACKED_FILE_BYTES)` returns an error. Every other operation the function reaches succeeds.
findings.why: Jev answered `applies` (0.96) when asked whether the requirement requires this call's failure not to reach the caller as a success, and `returns_success` (1.00) when asked what `read_baseline` returns under that failure. Both are Jev's readings and neither checks the other.

findings.quote: If reading an existing configuration file fails while checking whether a rule override disables a rule, that check must return an error to its caller. It must not return a successful result saying that the rule is not disabled.
findings.condition: Execution reaches the call `crate::atomic_file::read_to_string_capped(path, MAX_CONFIG_FILE_BYTES)` inside `raw_override_disables`. There, `crate::atomic_file::read_to_string_capped(path, MAX_CONFIG_FILE_BYTES)` returns an error. Every other operation the function reaches succeeds.
findings.why: Jev answered `applies` (1.00) when asked whether the requirement requires this call's failure not to reach the caller as a success, and `returns_success` (0.99) when asked what `raw_override_disables` returns under that failure. Both are Jev's readings and neither checks the other.
